svg.title: How one task flows through the six roles
svg.desc: The six roles are a person, an AI coordinator, AI workers, AI reviewers, the Runtime Pack and the project record. In step one, the person sets the goal, the scope and the budget; at named checkpoints (releases, budgets, pushes) the person decides, on the evidence the coordinator sends up. In step two, the coordinator gives each worker a brief. In step three, the workers change the code and report back. In step four, the coordinator re-runs the checks itself; a test that could never fail does not count. In step five, independent AI reviewers, starting fresh, challenge the claims and return findings; the coordinator sends those findings to the workers to be fixed. In step six, the coordinator reads and records each step in the project record, in files and Git. The Runtime Pack provides the versioned rules and checks and starts nothing by itself. Four of its rules: every report is re-run; significant changes get two fresh reviewers, one from a different vendor where available; every step is recorded; and nothing is released or pushed without a person.
